recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core follow-up is needed unless the work group later standardizes a different cross-language notation for matching any non-empty primitive string.
issue_request: FHIR-40563 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and asked to replace the R5 string regex `[ \r\n\t\S]+`, which rejected a Unicode whitespace-only string, and to use the same regex for markdown.
initial_application: No Jira-tagged implementation commit was found. Commit b4c3af0a97b6ef5d8db2c49745c9e98ff7ab0341, `fix string and markdown regex values`, changed `source/datatypes/primitives.xml` from the old string and markdown regexes to `^[\s\S]+$` for both.
additional_context: The datatype source is active through `source/fhir.ini` type-page routing to `datatypes`. Confluence minutes confirm the FHIR-I same-call persuasive-with-modification revote, and the Zulip thread explains that `.+` did not match the Unicode whitespace sample in Java while `[\s\S]+` did, so the current expression better captures the intended cross-line/non-empty behavior.
reconciliation: No source change was made. `source/datatypes/primitives.xml` currently has `^[\s\S]+$` for both string and markdown, and the old regex is absent from active source outside historical release snapshots.
